title: Frames Per Second (Textable, Numeric)
description: Target frame rate for video frame extraction
documentation:
## Purpose
Specifies a target frame rate (frames per second) for caps that decimate or sample video frames. The cap selects approximately `fps` frames per second from the source by emitting the first decoded frame whose presentation timestamp passes each `1/fps`-second boundary.

## When to use
Pass to [Extract Frames](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:extract-frames;in=media:video;out="media:image;png") (and its per-container variants) to subsample video into a manageable image stream. With no `--fps` argument the cap emits every decoded frame; with `--fps 1` the cap emits ~1 frame per second.

## Notes
Must be a positive finite number. Caps reject zero, negative, or non-finite values loudly rather than silently passing through every frame, since `--fps 0` is unambiguously a programmer error.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Numeric
Coercion marker indicating the value supports numeric operations (addition,
comparison, ordering). Independent of `textable`; a numeric value is often
also textable (an integer is encodable as text), but neither implies the
other in general.

The value supports numeric operations.
